honoursNote: Major honours include the top-flight league, FA Cup, League Cup, European Cup / Champions League, UEFA Cup, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup. Promotion and the Football League Super Cup are noted separately; Charity/Community Shields are excluded.

eras.summary: From the Second Division to champions of England and UEFA Cup winners. Shankly rebuilt Liverpool and established the foundations for the decades that followed.
eras.context: Promotion in 1962 was the starting point. The first FA Cup followed in 1965, before a renewed side won the league and UEFA Cup in 1973. His final season brought another FA Cup.

eras.summary: Six league titles and three European Cups in nine seasons. Paisley turned Shankly’s foundations into sustained success at home and across Europe.
eras.context: Liverpool won their first European Cup in Rome in 1977, retained it in 1978 and won it again in Paris in 1981. Paisley kept renewing the team, bringing in Dalglish, Souness, Hansen and Rush.

eras.summary: Fagan’s first season brought the league, European Cup and League Cup. Another Boot Room successor, he kept Liverpool at the summit of European football.
eras.context: The 1984 European Cup was won against Roma in their own stadium. Liverpool reached the final again in 1985, when the Heysel disaster cost 39 people their lives. Fagan had already decided to retire at the season’s end.

eras.summary: A league and FA Cup double as player-manager, followed by the exhilarating Barnes, Beardsley and Aldridge side. Dalglish delivered three league titles in his first spell.
eras.context: The 1987–88 champions gave Liverpool some of their most celebrated attacking football. Hillsborough in 1989 brought devastating loss to the club and its community. Liverpool won another title in 1990, before Dalglish resigned in February 1991.

eras.summary: A trusted Boot Room figure took temporary charge after Dalglish’s resignation. Moran held the team together while Liverpool sought a permanent successor.
eras.context: His ten-match caretaker spell included a remarkable 5–4 league win at Leeds. Graeme Souness then took over, with Moran returning to the coaching staff.

eras.summary: The 1992 FA Cup was the high point of a difficult period of change. Established champions gave way to a new generation as the Premier League began.
eras.context: Souness returned from Rangers to rebuild an ageing squad. Liverpool beat Sunderland at Wembley, while Steve McManaman, Jamie Redknapp and Robbie Fowler began to emerge. League results proved much harder to sustain.

eras.summary: Fowler and McManaman flourished in an adventurous Liverpool side. Evans restored attacking confidence and won the League Cup in his first full season.
eras.context: A 3–5–2 system helped Liverpool finish fourth and lift the 1995 League Cup. Stan Collymore joined Fowler in attack, but promising league challenges never became a title. Evans later shared the job with Gérard Houllier.

eras.summary: A short experiment in joint management bridged two eras. Evans and Houllier shared responsibility before Houllier took sole charge in November.
eras.context: The partnership lasted 18 competitive matches. A promising league start gave way to inconsistent results, and Evans left on 12 November 1998. This separate entry keeps that shared period distinct from either manager’s sole tenure.

eras.summary: Three cups in 2001 made Houllier’s rebuilding work tangible. A side shaped by Owen, Gerrard and Hyypiä returned Liverpool to regular European contention.
eras.context: The League Cup, FA Cup and UEFA Cup all came in 2001, followed by the UEFA Super Cup. Another League Cup arrived in 2003. Phil Thompson deputised during Houllier’s recovery from serious illness in 2001–02.

eras.context: Liverpool recovered from 3–0 down against Milan to win the 2005 Champions League on penalties. Another final followed in 2007. Gerrard and Torres then powered a title challenge that ended with second place in 2008–09.

eras.context: Appointed from Fulham in July 2010, Hodgson lasted just over six months. A win over Chelsea offered a high point, but poor domestic results continued. Kenny Dalglish returned in January 2011.

eras.summary: A thrilling title challenge defined Rodgers’ time at Anfield. Suárez, Sturridge and a young attacking side took Liverpool to second place in 2013–14.
eras.context: Rodgers arrived from Swansea with an emphasis on possession and developing players. The additions of Daniel Sturridge and Philippe Coutinho helped transform the attack. Rebuilding after Suárez’s departure proved difficult, and Rodgers left in October 2015.

eras.summary: European champions, world champions, then champions of England. Klopp’s pressing game and connection with supporters helped return Liverpool to the top.
eras.context: The 2019 Champions League was followed by Liverpool’s first league title in 30 years in 2020. Domestic cups followed in 2022 and 2024. Salah, Mané and Firmino led the attack, with Van Dijk and Alisson transforming the defence.

eras.summary: Slot won Liverpool’s twentieth league title in his first season. His two-year spell began with a successful transition from Klopp’s team.
eras.context: The 2024–25 Premier League title was the defining achievement of Slot’s tenure. He had arrived from Feyenoord and formally started on 1 June 2024. Liverpool announced his departure with immediate effect on 30 May 2026.
